headline: London Gatwick is first UK airport with robotic parking, launching in August
summary: Passengers drop their car in a private cabin, keep their keys, and autonomous robots handle parking and retrieval, enhancing efficiency and peace of mind.
details: London Gatwick is the first UK airport to introduce robotic parking, partnering with Stanley Robotics. The service is available to book now, with first customer journeys starting in August. Passengers can leave their car in a private drop-off cabin and keep their keys.

The system aims to get passengers from their car to the terminal more quickly by eliminating the need to search for a parking space. It also makes more efficient use of airport parking capacity by allowing cars to be parked closer together.

Passengers drive into an enclosed cabin near the South Terminal, scan their booking, and leave their vehicle. A Stanley Robotics autonomous robot then slides underneath the car, lifts it by its tyres, and transports it to a secure storage area.

Upon booking, passengers provide return flight details, enabling the system to monitor their arrival and have the vehicle ready in a collection cabin. Unlike traditional valet, passengers retain their keys, offering additional peace of mind.

On-site staff are available for emergency item retrieval if something is accidentally left in the vehicle after drop-off. This robotic system improves customer experience and maximizes parking density without requiring new infrastructure.

Stanley Robotics has successfully deployed similar autonomous parking systems internationally, with the Gatwick installation marking its first deployment at a UK airport. The service supports most standard passenger cars.

Oli Bedford from London Gatwick called it "a real game-changer," highlighting its quick, easy, and hassle-free nature. Stanley Robotics CEO Clément Boussard noted the technology will help address future parking demand as the airport grows.

The robotic parking service must be booked in advance; same-day drive-up parking is not available. The facility is within walking distance of the South Terminal, with a free shuttle bus also provided.

headline_marked: [[Htmx 4.0 launches exclusively on the Game Boy]], a first for a JavaScript library
headline: Htmx 4.0 launches exclusively on the Game Boy, a first for a JavaScript library
summary: The new version of the JavaScript library is presented as a retro-style Game Boy game, challenging players to "squish client-side JS down to size" and unlock the source code.
details: HTMX 4.0, the popular JavaScript library, has taken an unconventional route for its latest release, launching exclusively on the Nintendo Game Boy platform. This marks the first time a JavaScript library has been released in such a format, blending modern web development with retro gaming.

The release is presented as a game titled 'Golden Master,' offering four levels of 'pickle-collecting excitement.' Players are tasked with avoiding 'slop' and 'squishing client-side JS down to size' within the game's pixelated world.

The ultimate objective for players is to defeat a character named 'Warren.' Successfully completing this challenge will reportedly unlock the full HTMX 4.0 source code, turning the release into an interactive puzzle for developers.
